1.why: All nine screens are static, card-based layouts with no animations, moving images, or pop-ups, though the academic Logs panel adds some extra on-page clutter.

2.why: Primary actions are bold blue buttons, headings are large, and the security notice sits in a distinct green box, so key items are visually salient.

3.why: Each page presents a single task with one input field and one primary button, so the next needed action is easy to locate.

4.why: The flow spans nine steps requiring a 14-128 character password with four character classes, a long recovery token, and two different six-digit codes, which is a substantial amount to remember.

5.why: No password manager integration, autofill option, or 'remember me' checkbox is visible on any screen.

6.why: Nothing is saved or recognized for the user (the contact field starts empty and no remembered accounts or items are offered); only the repeated security banner is familiar.

7.why: Instructions are one or two short plain sentences per page and the privacy statement is three short bullets.

8.why: No error message appears in any of the nine screenshots, so whether errors describe problems and fixes cannot be confirmed.

9.why: The contact field gives a concrete example ('name@example.org or +15551234567') and format hints accompany the token, code, and password fields.

10.why: Only a single password-plus-code path exists with no alternatives like face login, though the few choices offered (simulated link vs. manual token entry) are labeled clearly.

11.why: Every screen offers at most one primary action and one secondary link, so the user is never confronted with many simultaneous choices.

12.why: Actions produce explicit outcome messages, e.g., 'recovery instructions have been prepared' and 'Privacy statement accepted... securely recorded.'

13.why: Short tips accompany new steps, such as 'Tokens are short-lived and can only be used once' and the password format requirement.

14.why: No error state, retry option, or 'resend code' link is shown in the screenshots, so ease of trying again after a mistake cannot be verified.

15.why: The header, card layout, button styling, and green safe-authentication notice are identical across all nine steps, providing strong consistency.
